The **2020 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2019–20 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Champions_League "2019–20 UEFA Champions League"), the 65th season of Europe's premier club football tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), and the 28th season since it was re-branded from the [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") to the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). It was played on 23 August 2020 at the [Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz") in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), Portugal, between French club [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), in their first European Cup final, and German club [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") having returned to the final for the first time since [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2013 UEFA Champions League final"). The match was held [behind closed doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind_closed_doors_(sport) "Behind closed doors (sport)") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Europe "COVID-19 pandemic in Europe").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-uefa_behind_closed_doors-6)

Originally, it had been scheduled to be played at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, on 30 May 2020.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-auto-7) On 17 June 2020, the UEFA Executive Committee chose to relocate the final to Lisbon as part of a "final-eight tournament" consisting of single-match knockout ties played in two stadiums across the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-8) The match was the first European premier tournament final to be played on a Sunday, and the first since [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final") to not be played on a Saturday. It was also the first final of the competition to be played after June.

Bayern Munich won the final 1–0 thanks to a 59th-minute goal scored by former Paris Saint-Germain player [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman") assisted by Joshua Kimmich, who was later selected as [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_the_match "Man of the match").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-MOTM-1) Bayern secured their sixth European Cup title and second [continental treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)"), becoming the second European men's football team to win the continental treble twice.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-9) Bayern also became the first team to claim any European competition [with a 100% winning record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_competition_records_and_statistics#Ranking_main_European_club_competitions'_winning_club_sides_by_winning_percentage "UEFA club competition records and statistics").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-BBC_final-10) As winners, they earned the right to play against the winners of the [2019–20 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Europa_League "2019–20 UEFA Europa League"), [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"), in the [2020 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Super_Cup "2020 UEFA Super Cup"), and also qualified for the [2020 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2020 FIFA Club World Cup") in Qatar; Bayern went on to win both and complete a historic [sextuple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sextuple_(association_football) "Sextuple (association football)") (six trophies in a year).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-11)

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

For the details on the selection of Istanbul as the original host for the final, see [2021 UEFA Champions League final §Host selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_UEFA_Champions_League_final#Host_selection "2021 UEFA Champions League final").

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/LuzLissabon.jpg/500px-LuzLissabon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LuzLissabon.jpg)

The [Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz") in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon") hosted the final.

The final was originally scheduled to be played at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, on 30 May 2020.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-venue-12) However, UEFA announced on 23 March 2020 that the final was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-auto-7) On 17 June 2020, the UEFA Executive Committee chose to relocate the final to Lisbon as part of a "final-eight tournament" consisting of single-match knockout ties played in two stadiums across the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-8) The match was the first European Cup/Champions League final to be played on a Sunday and the first since [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final") to not be played on a Saturday. It was also the first final of the competition to be played after June.

The UEFA Executive Committee chose the [Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz"), officially known as the Estádio do Sport Lisboa e Benfica, in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon") as the final venue at their meeting on 17 June 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-8) This is the second UEFA Champions League final hosted at the stadium; the first was in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2014 UEFA Champions League final"), when [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") secured their 10th title by beating [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") 4–1 in the first final between [teams from the same city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_derby "Madrid derby").

The home stadium of Portuguese Primeira Liga side [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") since 2003, it was newly built to host five matches of [UEFA Euro 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2004 "UEFA Euro 2004"), including the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2004_Final "UEFA Euro 2004 Final"). Before its demolition in 2003, to make way for the new 65,000-capacity ground, the [original Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz_(1954) "Estádio da Luz (1954)") hosted the [1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), where [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen") beat [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") 2–0, and the second leg of the [1983 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_UEFA_Cup_final "1983 UEFA Cup final"), where [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.S.C._Anderlecht "R.S.C. Anderlecht") secured a 1–1 draw with Benfica to lift the trophy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-previous_finals-13)

Lisbon had also staged a European Cup final in [1967](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_final "1967 European Cup final"), when Scottish side [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") beat [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") of Italy 2–1 at the [Estádio Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Nacional "Estádio Nacional"). The Portuguese capital also hosted the [2005 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final "2005 UEFA Cup final") at the [Estádio José Alvalade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Jos%C3%A9_Alvalade "Estádio José Alvalade"), home of Benfica's local rivals and finalists [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP"), who lost 3–1 to [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-previous_finals-13)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

[Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC") (PSG) reached their first European Cup/Champions League final, becoming the fifth finalist representing France and the 41st overall. They entered the final having played 110 prior matches in the European Cup and Champions League, the most for a final debutant, surpassing [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.")'s record of 90 matches prior to their final debut in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2006 UEFA Champions League final").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-14) The match was the seventh final to feature a French team, and the first since Monaco in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2004 UEFA Champions League final"). [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") were the only French club to have won the competition, doing so in [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1993 UEFA Champions League final").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF_EC-15) The match was the fourth time Paris Saint-Germain have appeared in the final of a UEFA competition, having previously appeared in two consecutive finals of the [UEFA Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup"). The club won the [1996 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1996 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final") 1–0 against [Rapid Wien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_Rapid_Wien "SK Rapid Wien"), before losing 1–0 against [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") while attempting to defend their title in [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1997 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ECWC-16) PSG also featured in the [1996 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Super_Cup "1996 UEFA Super Cup"), losing 9–2 on aggregate to [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17) Paris were attempting to become the first French team to complete a continental treble, having won [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Ligue_1 "2019–20 Ligue 1"), which was awarded to them based on PPG ratio as the season was ended prematurely due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_France "COVID-19 pandemic in France"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) and the [Coupe de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Coupe_de_France "2019–20 Coupe de France").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-19) The club also won the final season of the [Coupe de la Ligue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Coupe_de_la_Ligue "2019–20 Coupe de la Ligue") ([league cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_cup "League cup")) and the [Trophée des Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Troph%C3%A9e_des_Champions "2019 Trophée des Champions") ([super cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_cup "Super cup")),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21) thus winning all four domestic titles, though only the main domestic cup competition was considered for a continental treble.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-22)

In eighteen matches, Paris Saint-Germain had a record of eleven wins, two draws and five losses against German clubs in European competition. PSG won all four prior knockout ties in which they met German opposition, including earlier in the season against [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") in the round of 16 and [RB Leipzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Leipzig "RB Leipzig") in the semi-finals.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-press_kit-23)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Hans-Dieter_Flick%2C_Germany_national_football_team_%2803%29.jpg/250px-Hans-Dieter_Flick%2C_Germany_national_football_team_%2803%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hans-Dieter_Flick,_Germany_national_football_team_(03).jpg)

Bayern Munich manager [Hansi Flick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hansi_Flick "Hansi Flick") appeared in his second European Cup final, having lost as a player with Bayern in [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_European_Cup_final "1987 European Cup final").

[Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") reached their eleventh European Cup/Champions League final, tying [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") for the second-most finals behind Real Madrid's 16. Most recently they appeared in the [2013 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2013 UEFA Champions League final"), in which they won 2–1 against archrivals Borussia Dortmund for their fifth title. In their prior finals, Bayern Munich won on four other occasions in [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_European_Cup_final "1974 European Cup final"), [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_European_Cup_final "1975 European Cup final"), [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_European_Cup_final "1976 European Cup final") and [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2001 UEFA Champions League final"), and lost in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_European_Cup_final "1982 European Cup final"), [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_European_Cup_final "1987 European Cup final"), [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final"), 2010 and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2012 UEFA Champions League final").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF_EC-15) The match was Bayern's 13th overall final in European competition, having won the [1967 European Cup Winners' Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1967 European Cup Winners' Cup Final") 1–0 after extra time against [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C.") and the [1996 UEFA Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Cup_Final "1996 UEFA Cup Final") 5–1 on aggregate against [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux "FC Girondins de Bordeaux").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ECWC-16)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UC-24) Bayern Munich were chasing a second treble in club history (previously doing so in [2012–13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_FC_Bayern_Munich_season "2012–13 FC Bayern Munich season")), having won the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Bundesliga "2019–20 Bundesliga") and [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_DFB-Pokal "2019–20 DFB-Pokal").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26) Entering the final, Bayern are on a 20-match winning streak and undefeated in 2020, having not lost in their prior 29 matches (winning 28 and drawing once).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-BBC_BAY_SF-27) With their semi-final win, Bayern also tied the record for the most consecutive wins in the competition proper, as well as the most wins from the start of the competition proper, with 10.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-28) Bayern are the second team to have entered the final with a perfect winning record, after Milan in 1993, who lost to the only French winners in competition history at that point, Marseille. Bayern are also the second club to reach the final after winning all six group stage matches, after the aforementioned Milan team in [1992–93](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_UEFA_Champions_League "1992–93 UEFA Champions League").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-29)

Bayern Munich scored 42 goals in 10 matches during the competition prior to the final, second only to Barcelona's record of 45 goals in 16 matches during the [1999–2000 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_UEFA_Champions_League "1999–2000 UEFA Champions League"). However, Bayern set a new record for the best goals per game ratio in competition history following their quarter-final (regardless of the outcome of the remainder of the competition), with 4.2 per match after their semi-final victory.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30) Entering the final, forward [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") scored 15 goals in 9 matches during the Champions League season, with only [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") having scored more in a single campaign (17 in [2013–14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") and 16 in [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Champions_League "2015–16 UEFA Champions League")). Lewandowski also tied [Ruud van Nistelrooy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_van_Nistelrooy "Ruud van Nistelrooy")'s mark from 2002–03 of scoring in nine consecutive Champions League matches, second only to Ronaldo's 11 from 2017–18.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-BBC_BAY_SF-27) Lewandowski and [Serge Gnabry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serge_Gnabry "Serge Gnabry") set a record for the most prolific scoring partnership in a season with 24 combined goals, surpassing the record of 23 between Ronaldo and [Gareth Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Bale "Gareth Bale") in 2013–14.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) Bayern manager [Hansi Flick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hansi_Flick "Hansi Flick") became the 15th individual to [appear in a Champions League final as both a player and manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Cup_and_UEFA_Champions_League_records_and_statistics#Final_and_winning_records "European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics"), having played for Bayern in their loss to [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto") in the 1987 final.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finals-32)

In 34 matches, Bayern Munich had a record of 19 wins, 5 draws and ten losses against French clubs in European competition. Bayern won six of their seven previous knockout ties against French opposition, two of which were finals, including their semi-final win over [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_Lyonnais "Olympique Lyonnais") to reach the 2020 final. Bayern's only loss was 3–2 on aggregate against [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne "AS Saint-Étienne") in the first round of the [1969–70 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969%E2%80%9370_European_Cup "1969–70 European Cup").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-press_kit-23)

The final was the ninth meeting between Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich, with a record of five wins for PSG and three wins for Bayern. The fixture was the first knockout match between the sides, with all their prior meetings occurring in the Champions League group stages. The sides most recently met in the [2017–18 UEFA Champions League group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_B "2017–18 UEFA Champions League group stage"); Paris won the first match 3–0 at home, while Bayern won the return match 3–1.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-33) As the sides were level on points, PSG won the group on head-to-head goal difference.

The match was the second European Cup final to feature a French and German team, after the 1976 final between Bayern and [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Saint-%C3%89tienne "A.S. Saint-Étienne").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF_EC-15) Overall, it was the fourth final in European competition between teams from France and Germany, also occurring in the 1992 European Cup Winners' Cup Final (between Werder Bremen and Monaco) and the 1996 UEFA Cup Final (between Bayern and Bordeaux). On all three occasions, German teams were victorious.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ECWC-16)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UC-24) It was also the third final in which both teams entered the match seeking a win to secure the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football) "Treble (association football)"), previously occurring in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final"), in which Bayern lost to Inter Milan, and [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2015 UEFA Champions League final"), when Barcelona defeated Juventus. The 1999 final, won by [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), also had both finalists seeking a treble, though Bayern had not yet contested their domestic cup final (which they ultimately lost). Both sides came into the final having won their domestic leagues the previous season, the first time this had happened since the [1998 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1998 UEFA Champions League final") between Juventus and Real Madrid.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34) It was also the first time since [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final") that both finalists won their domestic league in the previous and same season as reaching the final.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-36) The final was also the second to feature two German managers, after the 2013 edition with managers [Jürgen Klopp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp "Jürgen Klopp") for Borussia Dortmund and [Jupp Heynckes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupp_Heynckes "Jupp Heynckes") for Bayern Munich.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finals-32)

### Paris Saint-Germain

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Paris Saint-Germain")]

See also: [2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C._season "2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season")

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/PSG-Shakhter15_%282%29.jpg/250px-PSG-Shakhter15_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSG-Shakhter15_(2).jpg)

[Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Di_Mar%C3%ADa "Ángel Di María") of Paris Saint-Germain had the joint-most assists in the competition with six.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-top_scorers-37)

Paris Saint-Germain qualified for the Champions League group stage by winning the [2018–19 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ligue_1 "2018–19 Ligue 1") season, their sixth title in seven seasons and eighth overall French title. In the group stage, they were drawn into Group A alongside Real Madrid of Spain, record winners of the European Cup, as well as [Galatasaray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galatasaray_S.K._(football) "Galatasaray S.K. (football)") of Turkey and [Club Brugge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Brugge_KV "Club Brugge KV") of Belgium.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-GS_draw-38)

In the opening match of the group stage, Paris faced Real Madrid at the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes") and won 3–0 via a first-half brace from former Madrid player [Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Di_Mar%C3%ADa "Ángel Di María") and a second-half stoppage time goal from [Thomas Meunier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Meunier "Thomas Meunier").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39) On matchday 2, PSG won 1–0 against Galatasaray at the [Türk Telekom Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C3%BCrk_Telekom_Stadium "Türk Telekom Stadium") with a 52nd-minute goal from [Mauro Icardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Icardi "Mauro Icardi").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-40) Paris Saint-Germain continued their perfect start to the competition by defeating Club Brugge 5–0 at the [Jan Breydel Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Breydel_Stadium "Jan Breydel Stadium"), with a brace from Icardi and hat-trick from [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbapp%C3%A9 "Kylian Mbappé").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-41) In their home meeting against Brugge, Icardi scored PSG's lone goal in a 1–0 win to advance to the knockout stage.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42) On matchday 5, Paris recovered from a two-goal deficit to draw 2–2 at the [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") against Madrid and win Group A, with Mbappé and [Pablo Sarabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Sarabia "Pablo Sarabia")'s late goals offsetting a [Karim Benzema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karim_Benzema "Karim Benzema") brace.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43) In their final match, Paris Saint-Germain won 5–0 at home against Galatasaray to finish the group stage undefeated and having only conceded two goals.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44)

In the round of 16, PSG were drawn against German club Borussia Dortmund. In the first leg at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion"), Paris lost 2–1 with [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") scoring a goal in between a brace from [Erling Haaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erling_Haaland "Erling Haaland").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-45) The second leg was one of the last European matches played prior to the suspension of the competition due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), and took place [behind closed doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind_closed_doors_(sport) "Behind closed doors (sport)") on 11 March 2020. PSG won the match 2–0 with first-half goals from Neymar and [Juan Bernat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Bernat "Juan Bernat"), securing a 3–2 aggregate win for the Parisians and their first quarter-final appearance since the 2015–16 season.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46)

Paris were drawn against Italian club [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_BC "Atalanta BC") in the quarter-finals, who were participating in their debut season of the Champions League. The one-off tie was played on 12 August 2020 at the neutral Estádio da Luz. Atalanta took the lead in the first-half with a goal from [Mario Pašalić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Pa%C5%A1ali%C4%87 "Mario Pašalić"). PSG struggled to find an equaliser in the second half, until [Marquinhos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquinhos "Marquinhos") scored from close range in the 90th minute before substitute [Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Maxim_Choupo-Moting "Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting") scored three minutes later to snatch a late win for Paris. Paris Saint-Germain advanced to the Champions League semi-finals for the second time in their history after the [1994–95 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_UEFA_Champions_League "1994–95 UEFA Champions League").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-47)

In the semi-finals, Paris Saint-Germain faced RB Leipzig of Germany, who had qualified to the Champions League knockout stage for the first time in only their second season competing in the competition. Marquinhos and Di María scored in the first half at Estádio da Luz, while Bernat scored 11 minutes into the second period to earn PSG a 3–0 win and a spot in their first Champions League final.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48)

### Bayern Munich

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Bayern Munich")]

See also: [2019–20 FC Bayern Munich season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_FC_Bayern_Munich_season "2019–20 FC Bayern Munich season")

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Robert_Lewandowski123666.jpg/250px-Robert_Lewandowski123666.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Lewandowski123666.jpg)

Bayern striker [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") was the competition's leading scorer and joint-leading assister with 15 goals and 6 assists en route to the final.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-top_scorers-37)

Bayern Munich qualified directly for the group stage of the Champions League by winning the [2018–19 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Bundesliga "2018–19 Bundesliga"), their 7th consecutive and 29th overall German title. In the group stage, they were drawn into Group B alongside [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") of England, runners-up of the [previous Champions League season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"), as well as [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") of Greece and [Red Star Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Belgrade "Red Star Belgrade") of Serbia.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-GS_draw-38) The team began their season under Croatian manager [Niko Kovač](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niko_Kova%C4%8D "Niko Kovač").

In their first match, Bayern faced Red Star Belgrade in a home match at the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena") and won 3–0 with goals from [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman"), Robert Lewandowski and [Thomas Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_M%C3%BCller "Thomas Müller").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-49) In their second fixture against Tottenham at [Tottenham Hotspur Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_Stadium "Tottenham Hotspur Stadium"), Bayern won 7–2 with a goal from [Joshua Kimmich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Kimmich "Joshua Kimmich"), a brace from Lewandowski and four goals scored by Serge Gnabry.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-50) The result was the heaviest home loss by an English club in European competition.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-51) On matchday 3, Bayern faced Olympiacos at the [Karaiskakis Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaiskakis_Stadium "Karaiskakis Stadium") and recovered from a deficit to win 3–2 and maintain their lead in the group with a brace from Lewandowski followed by a curled goal from [Corentin Tolisso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corentin_Tolisso "Corentin Tolisso"), while [Youssef El-Arabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssef_El-Arabi "Youssef El-Arabi") and [Guilherme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_dos_Santos_Torres "Guilherme dos Santos Torres") scored for the Greek side.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-52)

However, as Bayern lost 5–1 to [Eintracht Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eintracht_Frankfurt "Eintracht Frankfurt") in the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga") on 2 November, manager Niko Kovač was sacked the following day and replaced by former assistant Hansi Flick on an interim basis.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-53) In Flick's first match in charge three days later, Bayern won the rematch against Olympiacos 2–0 via second-half goals from Lewandowski and [Ivan Perišić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Peri%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Ivan Perišić"), thus securing a spot in the knockout stage.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-54) On 26 November, Bayern Munich won 6–0 against Red Star Belgrade at the [Red Star Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Stadium "Red Star Stadium") to win Group B, with Lewandowski scoring four times between goals from [Leon Goretzka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Goretzka "Leon Goretzka") and Tolisso.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-55) In their final match, goals from Coman, Müller and [Philippe Coutinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Coutinho "Philippe Coutinho") earned Bayern a 3–1 home win against Tottenham Hotspur to finish with a perfect group stage record, while [Ryan Sessegnon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Sessegnon "Ryan Sessegnon") scored the only goal for the visitors.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-56) This was the seventh occasion a team finished the group stage with six wins from six, with Bayern the sixth club to do so. Following a successful spell as interim manager, Bayern announced on 22 December that Flick would remain manager until the end of season.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-57)

Bayern were drawn against English club [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") in the round of 16, with the last Champions League meeting between the sides taking place in the 2012 final. In the first leg away at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)"), Bayern won 3–0 via a brace from Gnabry followed by a tap-in from Lewandowski set-up by [Alphonso Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphonso_Davies "Alphonso Davies"). Chelsea defender [Marcos Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_Alonso_(footballer,_born_1990) "Marcos Alonso (footballer, born 1990)") was sent off late in the match, which was the club's heaviest home loss in European competition.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58) Following the match, Bayern chairman [Karl-Heinz Rummenigge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Rummenigge "Karl-Heinz Rummenigge") suggested Flick would stay permanently as manager.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-59) On 3 April, Flick signed a new contract with the club lasting until 2023.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-60) Due to the suspension of the competition due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the second leg was delayed from 18 March until 8 August 2020, and was played behind closed doors at the Allianz Arena. Bayern won the second meeting 4–1, with a Lewandowski brace and goals from Perišić and Tolisso earning a 7–1 victory on aggregate, while [Tammy Abraham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammy_Abraham "Tammy Abraham") scored for the visitors.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-61) The result was Chelsea's heaviest defeat in a two-legged European tie.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-62)

As a result of the draw, Bayern faced Spanish club Barcelona in the quarter-finals. The match, played at the Estádio da Luz, finished as an [8–2 win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona_2%E2%80%938_FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Barcelona 2–8 FC Bayern Munich") for Bayern Munich, with Perišić, Gnabry, Kimmich and Lewandowski scoring once each while Müller and Coutinho both earned braces. [David Alaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alaba "David Alaba") scored an early own goal for Barcelona, who netted their only other goal via a [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") strike in the 57th minute. For Bayern Munich, the result was the most goals scored by the club in a match during the Champions League era, and the second most for them in competition history after nine scored against [Omonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Omonia "AC Omonia") in the [1972–73 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972%E2%80%9373_European_Cup "1972–73 European Cup").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-63) The match was the first time Barcelona conceded six goals or more in European competition, and the first time they conceded four goals in the first half of a Champions League match.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64) It was Barcelona's heaviest defeat since 1951, when they lost 6–0 to [Espanyol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol") in the [1950–51 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950%E2%80%9351_La_Liga "1950–51 La Liga"), and the first time they conceded eight goals in a game since 1946, when they lost 8–0 to [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") in the [1946 Copa del Generalísimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946_Copa_del_General%C3%ADsimo#Round_of_16 "1946 Copa del Generalísimo").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-65)

Bayern met French club Lyon in the semi-finals of the competition at the Estádio José Alvalade, a rematch of the [2009–10 semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase#Semi-finals "2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"). Bayern won 3–0 with a brace from Gnabry followed by a late goal from Lewandowski to advance to their first Champions League final since 2013.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66)

### Identity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Identity")]

The original identity of the 2020 UEFA Champions League final was unveiled at the group-stage draw on 29 August 2019.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-67)

### Ambassador

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ambassador")]

The ambassador for the original Istanbul final was former Turkish international [Hamit Altıntop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamit_Alt%C4%B1ntop "Hamit Altıntop"),[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-68) who finished as runner-up in the [2009–10 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Champions_League "2009–10 UEFA Champions League") with Bayern Munich as well as winning the [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2003 UEFA Intertoto Cup") and [2004 UEFA Intertoto Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2004 UEFA Intertoto Cup") with [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04").

### Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Officials")]

On 20 August 2020, UEFA named Italian [Daniele Orsato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniele_Orsato "Daniele Orsato") as the referee for the final. Orsato had been a [FIFA referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_International_Referees_List "FIFA International Referees List") since 2010, and was previously the fourth official in the [2019 UEFA Europa League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2019 UEFA Europa League Final"). He was also an assistant video assistant referee in the [2018 FIFA World Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "2018 FIFA World Cup Final"). He was also an additional assistant referee at [UEFA Euro 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016") and a [video assistant referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_assistant_referee "Video assistant referee") at the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup"). He was joined by four of his fellow countrymen, with Lorenzo Manganelli and Alessandro Giallatini as assistant referees, [Massimiliano Irrati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimiliano_Irrati "Massimiliano Irrati") as the video assistant referee and [Marco Guida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Guida "Marco Guida") as the assistant VAR official. The fourth official was [Ovidiu Hațegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovidiu_Ha%C8%9Began "Ovidiu Hațegan") of Romania, while Spaniards Roberto Díaz Pérez del Palomar and [Alejandro Hernández Hernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Hern%C3%A1ndez "Alejandro Hernández Hernández") served as the offside and support VAR officials, respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-officials-2)

### Team selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Team selection")]

Each team made one change to their starting line-up following the semi-finals. After recovering from injury, Paris Saint-Germain first-choice goalkeeper [Keylor Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keylor_Navas "Keylor Navas") started in place of [Sergio Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Rico "Sergio Rico"). For Bayern Munich, manager Hansi Flick decided to replace Ivan Perišić, who had started in the three prior Champions League matches, with Paris native Kingsley Coman on the left wing. Centre-back [Jérôme Boateng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%B4me_Boateng "Jérôme Boateng") was also deemed fit to start for Bayern, having suffered a minor injury in the semi-final which required him to be substituted off at half-time.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ESPN-69)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Match")]

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Summary")]

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Kingsley_Coman_%282019%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Kingsley_Coman_%282019%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kingsley_Coman_(2019)_(cropped).jpg)

Bayern winger [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman") scored the only goal of the match in the 59th minute.

Paris Saint-Germain kicked off the match, though Bayern Munich began quickly in the opening stages, before Paris found their way into the game after 10 minutes. In the 18th minute, PSG had their first clear opportunity when Kylian Mbappé passed to Neymar on the left side of the penalty area, but his shot was blocked by the leg of Bayern goalkeeper [Manuel Neuer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Neuer "Manuel Neuer"). In the 22nd minute, Bayern forward Robert Lewandowski received the ball in the penalty area, swiveling and shooting the ball towards the goal which deflected off the inside of the left post and back into play. Two minutes later, Ángel Di María found himself with space in front of goal after a one-two with [Ander Herrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ander_Herrera "Ander Herrera"), but shot the ball over the crossbar of Neuer's goal. During the sequence, Bayern defender Jérôme Boateng injured himself, and had to be replaced by [Niklas Süle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niklas_S%C3%BCle "Niklas Süle"). Herrera had a drop-kick deflected wide of the Bayern goal in the 29th minute, while Lewandowski's 31st-minute dipping header was parried by PSG goalkeeper Keylor Navas. In the 45th minute, a misplaced pass by David Alaba in the Bayern back line fell in front of Mbappé, who played a one-two with Herrera before shooting the ball straight at Neuer when confronted by a clear opening on goal.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ESPN-69) In the following minute of first-half stoppage time, Kingsley Coman was hit on the shoulder by the arm of defender [Thilo Kehrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilo_Kehrer "Thilo Kehrer") and went down in the penalty area after cutting down the goal line. However, referee Daniele Orsato dismissed the Bayern appeals for a penalty, and blew for half-time with the match scoreless.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-70)

In the second half, Bayern scored the only goal in the 59th minute with a header by Coman, a PSG academy graduate. Thomas Müller laid a pass from Serge Gnabry back to right-back Joshua Kimmich, who crossed the ball from the right into the box towards the unmarked Coman at the far post, which was headed across the goal past Navas and into the right corner of the net. Following the goal, Bayern quickly created additional opportunities in the Parisian half, but were unable to capitalise on the chances. Bayern subsequently switched to a more defensive approach, and in the 70th minute Neuer made another save with his leg after Marquinhos found himself clear on goal following a pass from Ángel Di María into the left side of the penalty box. Three minutes later, Mbappé was caught on the back of his foot by Kimmich after cutting inside the Bayern penalty area, but referee Orsato again decided to not award a penalty. The final chance of the match came in stoppage time, when Mbappé ran down the inside-left channel and passed to Neymar on the left side of Bayern's penalty box, who turned sharply and shot wide of the far post, with substitute Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting's outstretched leg failing to meet the ball directly in front of the goal.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ESPN-69) Minutes later, the match ended as a 1–0 win for Bayern, securing the continental treble.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-71)

The **2020 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2019–20 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Champions_League "2019–20 UEFA Champions League"), the 65th season of Europe's premier club football tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), and the 28th season since it was re-branded from the [European Champion Clubs' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs'_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") to the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). It was played on 23 August 2020 at the [Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz") in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), Portugal, between French club [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), in their first European Cup final, and German club [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") having returned to the final for the first time since [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2013 UEFA Champions League final"). The match was held [behind closed doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind_closed_doors_(sport) "Behind closed doors (sport)") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Europe "COVID-19 pandemic in Europe").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-uefa_behind_closed_doors-6)

Originally, it had been scheduled to be played at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, on 30 May 2020.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-auto-7) On 17 June 2020, the UEFA Executive Committee chose to relocate the final to Lisbon as part of a "final-eight tournament" consisting of single-match knockout ties played in two stadiums across the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-8) The match was the first European premier tournament final to be played on a Sunday, and the first since [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final") to not be played on a Saturday. It was also the first final of the competition to be played after June.

Bayern Munich won the final 1–0 thanks to a 59th-minute goal scored by former Paris Saint-Germain player [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman") assisted by Joshua Kimmich, who was later selected as [man of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_the_match "Man of the match").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-MOTM-1) Bayern secured their sixth European Cup title and second [continental treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)"), becoming the second European men's football team to win the continental treble twice.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-9) Bayern also became the first team to claim any European competition [with a 100% winning record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_competition_records_and_statistics#Ranking_main_European_club_competitions'_winning_club_sides_by_winning_percentage "UEFA club competition records and statistics").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-BBC_final-10) As winners, they earned the right to play against the winners of the [2019–20 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Europa_League "2019–20 UEFA Europa League"), [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"), in the [2020 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Super_Cup "2020 UEFA Super Cup"), and also qualified for the [2020 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2020 FIFA Club World Cup") in Qatar; Bayern went on to win both and complete a historic [sextuple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sextuple_(association_football) "Sextuple (association football)") (six trophies in a year).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-11)

## Venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Venue")]

For the details on the selection of Istanbul as the original host for the final, see [2021 UEFA Champions League final §Host selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_UEFA_Champions_League_final#Host_selection "2021 UEFA Champions League final").

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/LuzLissabon.jpg/500px-LuzLissabon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LuzLissabon.jpg)

The [Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz") in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon") hosted the final.

The final was originally scheduled to be played at the [Atatürk Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atat%C3%BCrk_Olympic_Stadium "Atatürk Olympic Stadium") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, on 30 May 2020.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-venue-12) However, UEFA announced on 23 March 2020 that the final was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-auto-7) On 17 June 2020, the UEFA Executive Committee chose to relocate the final to Lisbon as part of a "final-eight tournament" consisting of single-match knockout ties played in two stadiums across the city.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-8) The match was the first European Cup/Champions League final to be played on a Sunday and the first since [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final") to not be played on a Saturday. It was also the first final of the competition to be played after June.

The UEFA Executive Committee chose the [Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz"), officially known as the Estádio do Sport Lisboa e Benfica, in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon") as the final venue at their meeting on 17 June 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ExCo_17_June-8) This is the second UEFA Champions League final hosted at the stadium; the first was in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2014 UEFA Champions League final"), when [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") secured their 10th title by beating [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") 4–1 in the first final between [teams from the same city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_derby "Madrid derby").

The home stadium of Portuguese Primeira Liga side [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") since 2003, it was newly built to host five matches of [UEFA Euro 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2004 "UEFA Euro 2004"), including the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2004_Final "UEFA Euro 2004 Final"). Before its demolition in 2003, to make way for the new 65,000-capacity ground, the [original Estádio da Luz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz_(1954) "Estádio da Luz (1954)") hosted the [1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_final "1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final"), where [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen") beat [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") 2–0, and the second leg of the [1983 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_UEFA_Cup_final "1983 UEFA Cup final"), where [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.S.C._Anderlecht "R.S.C. Anderlecht") secured a 1–1 draw with Benfica to lift the trophy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-previous_finals-13)

Lisbon had also staged a European Cup final in [1967](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_final "1967 European Cup final"), when Scottish side [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") beat [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") of Italy 2–1 at the [Estádio Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Nacional "Estádio Nacional"). The Portuguese capital also hosted the [2005 UEFA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_final "2005 UEFA Cup final") at the [Estádio José Alvalade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_Jos%C3%A9_Alvalade "Estádio José Alvalade"), home of Benfica's local rivals and finalists [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP"), who lost 3–1 to [CSKA Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-previous_finals-13)

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

[Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC") (PSG) reached their first European Cup/Champions League final, becoming the fifth finalist representing France and the 41st overall. They entered the final having played 110 prior matches in the European Cup and Champions League, the most for a final debutant, surpassing [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.")'s record of 90 matches prior to their final debut in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2006 UEFA Champions League final").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-14) The match was the seventh final to feature a French team, and the first since Monaco in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2004 UEFA Champions League final"). [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") were the only French club to have won the competition, doing so in [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1993 UEFA Champions League final").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF_EC-15) The match was the fourth time Paris Saint-Germain have appeared in the final of a UEFA competition, having previously appeared in two consecutive finals of the [UEFA Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup "UEFA Cup Winners' Cup"). The club won the [1996 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1996 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final") 1–0 against [Rapid Wien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_Rapid_Wien "SK Rapid Wien"), before losing 1–0 against [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") while attempting to defend their title in [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1997 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ECWC-16) PSG also featured in the [1996 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Super_Cup "1996 UEFA Super Cup"), losing 9–2 on aggregate to [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-17) Paris were attempting to become the first French team to complete a continental treble, having won [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Ligue_1 "2019–20 Ligue 1"), which was awarded to them based on PPG ratio as the season was ended prematurely due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_France "COVID-19 pandemic in France"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-18) and the [Coupe de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Coupe_de_France "2019–20 Coupe de France").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-19) The club also won the final season of the [Coupe de la Ligue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Coupe_de_la_Ligue "2019–20 Coupe de la Ligue") ([league cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_cup "League cup")) and the [Trophée des Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Troph%C3%A9e_des_Champions "2019 Trophée des Champions") ([super cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_cup "Super cup")),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-21) thus winning all four domestic titles, though only the main domestic cup competition was considered for a continental treble.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-22)

In eighteen matches, Paris Saint-Germain had a record of eleven wins, two draws and five losses against German clubs in European competition. PSG won all four prior knockout ties in which they met German opposition, including earlier in the season against [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") in the round of 16 and [RB Leipzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Leipzig "RB Leipzig") in the semi-finals.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-press_kit-23)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Hans-Dieter_Flick%2C_Germany_national_football_team_%2803%29.jpg/250px-Hans-Dieter_Flick%2C_Germany_national_football_team_%2803%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hans-Dieter_Flick,_Germany_national_football_team_(03).jpg)

Bayern Munich manager [Hansi Flick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hansi_Flick "Hansi Flick") appeared in his second European Cup final, having lost as a player with Bayern in [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_European_Cup_final "1987 European Cup final").

[Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") reached their eleventh European Cup/Champions League final, tying [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") for the second-most finals behind Real Madrid's 16. Most recently they appeared in the [2013 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2013 UEFA Champions League final"), in which they won 2–1 against archrivals Borussia Dortmund for their fifth title. In their prior finals, Bayern Munich won on four other occasions in [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_European_Cup_final "1974 European Cup final"), [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_European_Cup_final "1975 European Cup final"), [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_European_Cup_final "1976 European Cup final") and [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2001 UEFA Champions League final"), and lost in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_European_Cup_final "1982 European Cup final"), [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_European_Cup_final "1987 European Cup final"), [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1999 UEFA Champions League final"), 2010 and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2012 UEFA Champions League final").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF_EC-15) The match was Bayern's 13th overall final in European competition, having won the [1967 European Cup Winners' Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup_Final "1967 European Cup Winners' Cup Final") 1–0 after extra time against [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C.") and the [1996 UEFA Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_UEFA_Cup_Final "1996 UEFA Cup Final") 5–1 on aggregate against [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux "FC Girondins de Bordeaux").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ECWC-16)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UC-24) Bayern Munich were chasing a second treble in club history (previously doing so in [2012–13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_FC_Bayern_Munich_season "2012–13 FC Bayern Munich season")), having won the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Bundesliga "2019–20 Bundesliga") and [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_DFB-Pokal "2019–20 DFB-Pokal").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-26) Entering the final, Bayern are on a 20-match winning streak and undefeated in 2020, having not lost in their prior 29 matches (winning 28 and drawing once).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-BBC_BAY_SF-27) With their semi-final win, Bayern also tied the record for the most consecutive wins in the competition proper, as well as the most wins from the start of the competition proper, with 10.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-28) Bayern are the second team to have entered the final with a perfect winning record, after Milan in 1993, who lost to the only French winners in competition history at that point, Marseille. Bayern are also the second club to reach the final after winning all six group stage matches, after the aforementioned Milan team in [1992–93](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_UEFA_Champions_League "1992–93 UEFA Champions League").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-29)

Bayern Munich scored 42 goals in 10 matches during the competition prior to the final, second only to Barcelona's record of 45 goals in 16 matches during the [1999–2000 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_UEFA_Champions_League "1999–2000 UEFA Champions League"). However, Bayern set a new record for the best goals per game ratio in competition history following their quarter-final (regardless of the outcome of the remainder of the competition), with 4.2 per match after their semi-final victory.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-30) Entering the final, forward [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") scored 15 goals in 9 matches during the Champions League season, with only [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") having scored more in a single campaign (17 in [2013–14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") and 16 in [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Champions_League "2015–16 UEFA Champions League")). Lewandowski also tied [Ruud van Nistelrooy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_van_Nistelrooy "Ruud van Nistelrooy")'s mark from 2002–03 of scoring in nine consecutive Champions League matches, second only to Ronaldo's 11 from 2017–18.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-BBC_BAY_SF-27) Lewandowski and [Serge Gnabry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serge_Gnabry "Serge Gnabry") set a record for the most prolific scoring partnership in a season with 24 combined goals, surpassing the record of 23 between Ronaldo and [Gareth Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Bale "Gareth Bale") in 2013–14.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-31) Bayern manager [Hansi Flick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hansi_Flick "Hansi Flick") became the 15th individual to [appear in a Champions League final as both a player and manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Cup_and_UEFA_Champions_League_records_and_statistics#Final_and_winning_records "European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics"), having played for Bayern in their loss to [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto") in the 1987 final.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finals-32)

In 34 matches, Bayern Munich had a record of 19 wins, 5 draws and ten losses against French clubs in European competition. Bayern won six of their seven previous knockout ties against French opposition, two of which were finals, including their semi-final win over [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_Lyonnais "Olympique Lyonnais") to reach the 2020 final. Bayern's only loss was 3–2 on aggregate against [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne "AS Saint-Étienne") in the first round of the [1969–70 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969%E2%80%9370_European_Cup "1969–70 European Cup").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-press_kit-23)

The final was the ninth meeting between Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich, with a record of five wins for PSG and three wins for Bayern. The fixture was the first knockout match between the sides, with all their prior meetings occurring in the Champions League group stages. The sides most recently met in the [2017–18 UEFA Champions League group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_B "2017–18 UEFA Champions League group stage"); Paris won the first match 3–0 at home, while Bayern won the return match 3–1.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-33) As the sides were level on points, PSG won the group on head-to-head goal difference.

The match was the second European Cup final to feature a French and German team, after the 1976 final between Bayern and [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Saint-%C3%89tienne "A.S. Saint-Étienne").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-RSSSF_EC-15) Overall, it was the fourth final in European competition between teams from France and Germany, also occurring in the 1992 European Cup Winners' Cup Final (between Werder Bremen and Monaco) and the 1996 UEFA Cup Final (between Bayern and Bordeaux). On all three occasions, German teams were victorious.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ECWC-16)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-UC-24) It was also the third final in which both teams entered the match seeking a win to secure the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football) "Treble (association football)"), previously occurring in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final"), in which Bayern lost to Inter Milan, and [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2015 UEFA Champions League final"), when Barcelona defeated Juventus. The 1999 final, won by [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), also had both finalists seeking a treble, though Bayern had not yet contested their domestic cup final (which they ultimately lost). Both sides came into the final having won their domestic leagues the previous season, the first time this had happened since the [1998 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1998 UEFA Champions League final") between Juventus and Real Madrid.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-34) It was also the first time since [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_final "1994 UEFA Champions League final") that both finalists won their domestic league in the previous and same season as reaching the final.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-36) The final was also the second to feature two German managers, after the 2013 edition with managers [Jürgen Klopp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp "Jürgen Klopp") for Borussia Dortmund and [Jupp Heynckes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupp_Heynckes "Jupp Heynckes") for Bayern Munich.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-finals-32)
