### Paris Saint-Germain

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Paris Saint-Germain")]

See also: [2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C._season "2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season")

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/PSG-Shakhter15_%282%29.jpg/250px-PSG-Shakhter15_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSG-Shakhter15_(2).jpg)

[Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Di_Mar%C3%ADa "Ángel Di María") of Paris Saint-Germain had the joint-most assists in the competition with six.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-top_scorers-37)

Paris Saint-Germain qualified for the Champions League group stage by winning the [2018–19 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ligue_1 "2018–19 Ligue 1") season, their sixth title in seven seasons and eighth overall French title. In the group stage, they were drawn into Group A alongside Real Madrid of Spain, record winners of the European Cup, as well as [Galatasaray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galatasaray_S.K._(football) "Galatasaray S.K. (football)") of Turkey and [Club Brugge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Brugge_KV "Club Brugge KV") of Belgium.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-GS_draw-38)

In the opening match of the group stage, Paris faced Real Madrid at the [Parc des Princes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_des_Princes "Parc des Princes") and won 3–0 via a first-half brace from former Madrid player [Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Di_Mar%C3%ADa "Ángel Di María") and a second-half stoppage time goal from [Thomas Meunier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Meunier "Thomas Meunier").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-39) On matchday 2, PSG won 1–0 against Galatasaray at the [Türk Telekom Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C3%BCrk_Telekom_Stadium "Türk Telekom Stadium") with a 52nd-minute goal from [Mauro Icardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Icardi "Mauro Icardi").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-40) Paris Saint-Germain continued their perfect start to the competition by defeating Club Brugge 5–0 at the [Jan Breydel Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Breydel_Stadium "Jan Breydel Stadium"), with a brace from Icardi and hat-trick from [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbapp%C3%A9 "Kylian Mbappé").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-41) In their home meeting against Brugge, Icardi scored PSG's lone goal in a 1–0 win to advance to the knockout stage.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-42) On matchday 5, Paris recovered from a two-goal deficit to draw 2–2 at the [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") against Madrid and win Group A, with Mbappé and [Pablo Sarabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Sarabia "Pablo Sarabia")'s late goals offsetting a [Karim Benzema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karim_Benzema "Karim Benzema") brace.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-43) In their final match, Paris Saint-Germain won 5–0 at home against Galatasaray to finish the group stage undefeated and having only conceded two goals.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-44)

In the round of 16, PSG were drawn against German club Borussia Dortmund. In the first leg at the [Westfalenstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfalenstadion "Westfalenstadion"), Paris lost 2–1 with [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") scoring a goal in between a brace from [Erling Haaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erling_Haaland "Erling Haaland").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-45) The second leg was one of the last European matches played prior to the suspension of the competition due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), and took place [behind closed doors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind_closed_doors_(sport) "Behind closed doors (sport)") on 11 March 2020. PSG won the match 2–0 with first-half goals from Neymar and [Juan Bernat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Bernat "Juan Bernat"), securing a 3–2 aggregate win for the Parisians and their first quarter-final appearance since the 2015–16 season.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-46)

Paris were drawn against Italian club [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_BC "Atalanta BC") in the quarter-finals, who were participating in their debut season of the Champions League. The one-off tie was played on 12 August 2020 at the neutral Estádio da Luz. Atalanta took the lead in the first-half with a goal from [Mario Pašalić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Pa%C5%A1ali%C4%87 "Mario Pašalić"). PSG struggled to find an equaliser in the second half, until [Marquinhos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquinhos "Marquinhos") scored from close range in the 90th minute before substitute [Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Maxim_Choupo-Moting "Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting") scored three minutes later to snatch a late win for Paris. Paris Saint-Germain advanced to the Champions League semi-finals for the second time in their history after the [1994–95 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_UEFA_Champions_League "1994–95 UEFA Champions League").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-47)

In the semi-finals, Paris Saint-Germain faced RB Leipzig of Germany, who had qualified to the Champions League knockout stage for the first time in only their second season competing in the competition. Marquinhos and Di María scored in the first half at Estádio da Luz, while Bernat scored 11 minutes into the second period to earn PSG a 3–0 win and a spot in their first Champions League final.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-48)

### Bayern Munich

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Bayern Munich")]

See also: [2019–20 FC Bayern Munich season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_FC_Bayern_Munich_season "2019–20 FC Bayern Munich season")

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Robert_Lewandowski123666.jpg/250px-Robert_Lewandowski123666.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Lewandowski123666.jpg)

Bayern striker [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") was the competition's leading scorer and joint-leading assister with 15 goals and 6 assists en route to the final.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-top_scorers-37)

Bayern Munich qualified directly for the group stage of the Champions League by winning the [2018–19 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Bundesliga "2018–19 Bundesliga"), their 7th consecutive and 29th overall German title. In the group stage, they were drawn into Group B alongside [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") of England, runners-up of the [previous Champions League season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"), as well as [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") of Greece and [Red Star Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Belgrade "Red Star Belgrade") of Serbia.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-GS_draw-38) The team began their season under Croatian manager [Niko Kovač](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niko_Kova%C4%8D "Niko Kovač").

In their first match, Bayern faced Red Star Belgrade in a home match at the [Allianz Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allianz_Arena "Allianz Arena") and won 3–0 with goals from [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman"), Robert Lewandowski and [Thomas Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_M%C3%BCller "Thomas Müller").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-49) In their second fixture against Tottenham at [Tottenham Hotspur Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_Stadium "Tottenham Hotspur Stadium"), Bayern won 7–2 with a goal from [Joshua Kimmich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Kimmich "Joshua Kimmich"), a brace from Lewandowski and four goals scored by Serge Gnabry.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-50) The result was the heaviest home loss by an English club in European competition.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-51) On matchday 3, Bayern faced Olympiacos at the [Karaiskakis Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaiskakis_Stadium "Karaiskakis Stadium") and recovered from a deficit to win 3–2 and maintain their lead in the group with a brace from Lewandowski followed by a curled goal from [Corentin Tolisso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corentin_Tolisso "Corentin Tolisso"), while [Youssef El-Arabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssef_El-Arabi "Youssef El-Arabi") and [Guilherme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_dos_Santos_Torres "Guilherme dos Santos Torres") scored for the Greek side.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-52)

However, as Bayern lost 5–1 to [Eintracht Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eintracht_Frankfurt "Eintracht Frankfurt") in the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga") on 2 November, manager Niko Kovač was sacked the following day and replaced by former assistant Hansi Flick on an interim basis.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-53) In Flick's first match in charge three days later, Bayern won the rematch against Olympiacos 2–0 via second-half goals from Lewandowski and [Ivan Perišić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Peri%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Ivan Perišić"), thus securing a spot in the knockout stage.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-54) On 26 November, Bayern Munich won 6–0 against Red Star Belgrade at the [Red Star Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Stadium "Red Star Stadium") to win Group B, with Lewandowski scoring four times between goals from [Leon Goretzka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Goretzka "Leon Goretzka") and Tolisso.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-55) In their final match, goals from Coman, Müller and [Philippe Coutinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Coutinho "Philippe Coutinho") earned Bayern a 3–1 home win against Tottenham Hotspur to finish with a perfect group stage record, while [Ryan Sessegnon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Sessegnon "Ryan Sessegnon") scored the only goal for the visitors.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-56) This was the seventh occasion a team finished the group stage with six wins from six, with Bayern the sixth club to do so. Following a successful spell as interim manager, Bayern announced on 22 December that Flick would remain manager until the end of season.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-57)

Bayern were drawn against English club [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") in the round of 16, with the last Champions League meeting between the sides taking place in the 2012 final. In the first leg away at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)"), Bayern won 3–0 via a brace from Gnabry followed by a tap-in from Lewandowski set-up by [Alphonso Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphonso_Davies "Alphonso Davies"). Chelsea defender [Marcos Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_Alonso_(footballer,_born_1990) "Marcos Alonso (footballer, born 1990)") was sent off late in the match, which was the club's heaviest home loss in European competition.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58) Following the match, Bayern chairman [Karl-Heinz Rummenigge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Rummenigge "Karl-Heinz Rummenigge") suggested Flick would stay permanently as manager.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-59) On 3 April, Flick signed a new contract with the club lasting until 2023.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-60) Due to the suspension of the competition due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the second leg was delayed from 18 March until 8 August 2020, and was played behind closed doors at the Allianz Arena. Bayern won the second meeting 4–1, with a Lewandowski brace and goals from Perišić and Tolisso earning a 7–1 victory on aggregate, while [Tammy Abraham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammy_Abraham "Tammy Abraham") scored for the visitors.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-61) The result was Chelsea's heaviest defeat in a two-legged European tie.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-62)

As a result of the draw, Bayern faced Spanish club Barcelona in the quarter-finals. The match, played at the Estádio da Luz, finished as an [8–2 win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona_2%E2%80%938_FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Barcelona 2–8 FC Bayern Munich") for Bayern Munich, with Perišić, Gnabry, Kimmich and Lewandowski scoring once each while Müller and Coutinho both earned braces. [David Alaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alaba "David Alaba") scored an early own goal for Barcelona, who netted their only other goal via a [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") strike in the 57th minute. For Bayern Munich, the result was the most goals scored by the club in a match during the Champions League era, and the second most for them in competition history after nine scored against [Omonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Omonia "AC Omonia") in the [1972–73 European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972%E2%80%9373_European_Cup "1972–73 European Cup").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-63) The match was the first time Barcelona conceded six goals or more in European competition, and the first time they conceded four goals in the first half of a Champions League match.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64) It was Barcelona's heaviest defeat since 1951, when they lost 6–0 to [Espanyol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol") in the [1950–51 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950%E2%80%9351_La_Liga "1950–51 La Liga"), and the first time they conceded eight goals in a game since 1946, when they lost 8–0 to [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") in the [1946 Copa del Generalísimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946_Copa_del_General%C3%ADsimo#Round_of_16 "1946 Copa del Generalísimo").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-65)

Bayern met French club Lyon in the semi-finals of the competition at the Estádio José Alvalade, a rematch of the [2009–10 semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase#Semi-finals "2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"). Bayern won 3–0 with a brace from Gnabry followed by a late goal from Lewandowski to advance to their first Champions League final since 2013.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66)

### Ambassador

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ambassador")]

The ambassador for the original Istanbul final was former Turkish international [Hamit Altıntop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamit_Alt%C4%B1ntop "Hamit Altıntop"),[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-68) who finished as runner-up in the [2009–10 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Champions_League "2009–10 UEFA Champions League") with Bayern Munich as well as winning the [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2003 UEFA Intertoto Cup") and [2004 UEFA Intertoto Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2004 UEFA Intertoto Cup") with [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04").

### Officials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Officials")]

On 20 August 2020, UEFA named Italian [Daniele Orsato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniele_Orsato "Daniele Orsato") as the referee for the final. Orsato had been a [FIFA referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_International_Referees_List "FIFA International Referees List") since 2010, and was previously the fourth official in the [2019 UEFA Europa League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2019 UEFA Europa League Final"). He was also an assistant video assistant referee in the [2018 FIFA World Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "2018 FIFA World Cup Final"). He was also an additional assistant referee at [UEFA Euro 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016") and a [video assistant referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_assistant_referee "Video assistant referee") at the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup"). He was joined by four of his fellow countrymen, with Lorenzo Manganelli and Alessandro Giallatini as assistant referees, [Massimiliano Irrati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimiliano_Irrati "Massimiliano Irrati") as the video assistant referee and [Marco Guida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Guida "Marco Guida") as the assistant VAR official. The fourth official was [Ovidiu Hațegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovidiu_Ha%C8%9Began "Ovidiu Hațegan") of Romania, while Spaniards Roberto Díaz Pérez del Palomar and [Alejandro Hernández Hernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Hern%C3%A1ndez "Alejandro Hernández Hernández") served as the offside and support VAR officials, respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-officials-2)

### Team selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Team selection")]

Each team made one change to their starting line-up following the semi-finals. After recovering from injury, Paris Saint-Germain first-choice goalkeeper [Keylor Navas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keylor_Navas "Keylor Navas") started in place of [Sergio Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Rico "Sergio Rico"). For Bayern Munich, manager Hansi Flick decided to replace Ivan Perišić, who had started in the three prior Champions League matches, with Paris native Kingsley Coman on the left wing. Centre-back [Jérôme Boateng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%B4me_Boateng "Jérôme Boateng") was also deemed fit to start for Bayern, having suffered a minor injury in the semi-final which required him to be substituted off at half-time.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ESPN-69)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Match")]

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Summary")]

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Kingsley_Coman_%282019%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Kingsley_Coman_%282019%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kingsley_Coman_(2019)_(cropped).jpg)

Bayern winger [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman") scored the only goal of the match in the 59th minute.

Paris Saint-Germain kicked off the match, though Bayern Munich began quickly in the opening stages, before Paris found their way into the game after 10 minutes. In the 18th minute, PSG had their first clear opportunity when Kylian Mbappé passed to Neymar on the left side of the penalty area, but his shot was blocked by the leg of Bayern goalkeeper [Manuel Neuer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Neuer "Manuel Neuer"). In the 22nd minute, Bayern forward Robert Lewandowski received the ball in the penalty area, swiveling and shooting the ball towards the goal which deflected off the inside of the left post and back into play. Two minutes later, Ángel Di María found himself with space in front of goal after a one-two with [Ander Herrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ander_Herrera "Ander Herrera"), but shot the ball over the crossbar of Neuer's goal. During the sequence, Bayern defender Jérôme Boateng injured himself, and had to be replaced by [Niklas Süle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niklas_S%C3%BCle "Niklas Süle"). Herrera had a drop-kick deflected wide of the Bayern goal in the 29th minute, while Lewandowski's 31st-minute dipping header was parried by PSG goalkeeper Keylor Navas. In the 45th minute, a misplaced pass by David Alaba in the Bayern back line fell in front of Mbappé, who played a one-two with Herrera before shooting the ball straight at Neuer when confronted by a clear opening on goal.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ESPN-69) In the following minute of first-half stoppage time, Kingsley Coman was hit on the shoulder by the arm of defender [Thilo Kehrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilo_Kehrer "Thilo Kehrer") and went down in the penalty area after cutting down the goal line. However, referee Daniele Orsato dismissed the Bayern appeals for a penalty, and blew for half-time with the match scoreless.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-70)

In the second half, Bayern scored the only goal in the 59th minute with a header by Coman, a PSG academy graduate. Thomas Müller laid a pass from Serge Gnabry back to right-back Joshua Kimmich, who crossed the ball from the right into the box towards the unmarked Coman at the far post, which was headed across the goal past Navas and into the right corner of the net. Following the goal, Bayern quickly created additional opportunities in the Parisian half, but were unable to capitalise on the chances. Bayern subsequently switched to a more defensive approach, and in the 70th minute Neuer made another save with his leg after Marquinhos found himself clear on goal following a pass from Ángel Di María into the left side of the penalty box. Three minutes later, Mbappé was caught on the back of his foot by Kimmich after cutting inside the Bayern penalty area, but referee Orsato again decided to not award a penalty. The final chance of the match came in stoppage time, when Mbappé ran down the inside-left channel and passed to Neymar on the left side of Bayern's penalty box, who turned sharply and shot wide of the far post, with substitute Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting's outstretched leg failing to meet the ball directly in front of the goal.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-ESPN-69) Minutes later, the match ended as a 1–0 win for Bayern, securing the continental treble.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-71)

**Arrigo Sacchi** (born 1 April 1946) is an Italian former [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") executive and manager, best known for having managed [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") and the [Italy national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"). Regarded as one of the greatest managers of all time,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatestmanagers-2) his Milan side (1987–1991) is widely regarded to be one of the greatest club squads of all time.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-5)

Sacchi won the [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") title in his [debut season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987%E2%80%9388_Serie_A "1987–88 Serie A") and then dominated European football by winning back to back [European Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_final "1989 European Cup final") and [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final "1990 European Cup final"). From 1991 to 1996, he was head coach of Italy and led them to the [1994 FIFA World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1994 FIFA World Cup final"), where they lost to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in a penalty shoot-out.

Sacchi was never a professional football player and, for many years, worked as a shoe salesman. This led to his famous quote directed at those who questioned his qualifications: "I never realised that in order to become a jockey you have to have been a horse first."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-No_experience_required-6) Another famous Sacchi quote is that "football is the most important of the least important things in life".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]

Sacchi had grown up watching attacking sides, such as [Budapest Honvéd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest_Honv%C3%A9d_FC "Budapest Honvéd FC"), [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F."), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") and the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team "Netherlands national football team"). He started his career managing his local club, Baracca Lugo, because he was not good enough to play for them. Of the challenge he faced, Sacchi said, "I was twenty-six, my goalkeeper was thirty-nine and my centre-forward was thirty-two. I had to win them over." He next coached at Bellaria before joining [Cesena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Cesena "AC Cesena"), who were in the [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B"), as a youth team coach. He then took over at [Rimini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimini_Calcio_FC "Rimini Calcio FC"), who were playing in the [Serie C1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_C1 "Serie C1"), and almost led them to a title.

He received his breakthrough when he moved to [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") as a youth coach. His achievements with the youth team earned interest from [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913"), who were then playing in Serie C1. He led Parma to promotion in his first season, and in the following season took them to within 3 points of promotion to [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A"). Of greater importance to his time at Parma, however, was the team's performance in the [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppa_Italia "Coppa Italia"); they beat [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") 1–0 in the group stages, and beat them again 1–0 on aggregate in the first knockout round. This was enough to attract interest from Milan club owner [Silvio Berlusconi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silvio_Berlusconi "Silvio Berlusconi"), who promptly appointed Sacchi as manager.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-gazzettadiparma-8)

### AC Milan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: AC Milan")]

In Milan, Sacchi again faced problems of credibility. The press argued that such an inadequate player could never go on to be a successful coach, and that even Berlusconi – who had played football at amateur level – was probably a better player. Sacchi wittily replied, "I never realised that in order to become a jockey you have to have been a horse first."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-No_experience_required-6) Sacchi was an instant success at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"), leading Milan to its first [Serie A title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Italian_football_champions "List of Italian football champions") in nine years in his [debut season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987%E2%80%9388_Serie_A "1987–88 Serie A"), following up the league title with a [Supercoppa Italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercoppa_Italiana "Supercoppa Italiana") in [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Supercoppa_Italiana "1988 Supercoppa Italiana").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9)

Sacchi's success at Milan gained him two back-to-back [European Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9) The success he gained was largely attributed to the Dutch trio he had purchased: [Marco van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_van_Basten "Marco van Basten"), [Ruud Gullit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_Gullit "Ruud Gullit") and [Frank Rijkaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rijkaard "Frank Rijkaard"). However, other great players such as [Roberto Donadoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Donadoni "Roberto Donadoni"), as well as the defensive back four of [Franco Baresi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Baresi "Franco Baresi"), [Alessandro Costacurta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Costacurta "Alessandro Costacurta"), [Mauro Tassotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Tassotti "Mauro Tassotti") and [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini"), were also key to his success.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)

The first European Cup final in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_final "1989 European Cup final") was against [Steaua București](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Steaua_Bucure%C8%99ti "FC Steaua București"), who were beaten 4–0. Gullit and Van Basten scored two goals each and Milan lifted the [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988%E2%80%9389_European_Cup "1988–89 European Cup") for the first time in over 20 years. En route to the final, Milan had dispatched [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F.") 6–1 on aggregate in the semi-final. The quarter-final against [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen") was a tight affair; Milan only went through 1–0 on aggregate thanks to a Van Basten penalty. The second round was shrouded in controversy. Donadoni had his life saved only through the quick-thinking of the [Red Star Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Belgrade "Red Star Belgrade") physio, who broke his jaw to make a passage for oxygen to reach his lungs after he had suffered a bad foul and lay unconscious. The first leg ended in a 1–1 draw, and the second leg was called off in the 64th minute and rescheduled to be replayed the next day due to the thick fog (Milan was losing 0–1 at the moment). Milan eventually progressed following a penalty shoot-out.

Although the team was not as strong as they had been in the previous season, they were victorious again in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_European_Cup "1989–90 European Cup"). After victories against [HJK Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsingin_Jalkapalloklubi "Helsingin Jalkapalloklubi"), Real Madrid and [KV Mechelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KV_Mechelen "KV Mechelen"), Milan defeated German [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") in the semi-final, thanks to an [away goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goal_rule "Away goal rule"). In the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final "1990 European Cup final") Frank Rijkaard scored the only goal of the game through a Van Basten assist to conquer [Sven-Göran Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven-G%C3%B6ran_Eriksson "Sven-Göran Eriksson")'s [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica"). By winning the final, Milan became the first team which retained the title since [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979%E2%80%9380_European_Cup "1979–80 European Cup"), and the last team to do so until Real Madrid would manage to achieve this feat 27 years later. Sacchi would also capture back to back [European Super Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup "UEFA Super Cup") and [Intercontinental Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960%E2%80%932004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") in 1989 and 1990, and would lead Milan to the final of the [1989–90 Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_Coppa_Italia "1989–90 Coppa Italia"), where they were defeated by [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC"). The following season saw them defeated by [eventual runners-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_European_Cup "1990–91 European Cup")[Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") in the quarter-final, and finish second in [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_Serie_A "1990–91 Serie A") behind [Sampdoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Sampdoria "UC Sampdoria"), while they were eliminated in the semi-finals of the [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_Coppa_Italia "1990–91 Coppa Italia") by eventual champions [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma"). This was Sacchi's last season with _i Rossoneri_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9)

### Italy national team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Italy national team")]

In November 1991, Sacchi was appointed manager of the [Italy national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"), replacing [Azeglio Vicini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azeglio_Vicini "Azeglio Vicini"). Sacchi based his Italian selection predominantly on Milan players, especially in the defensive line, which featured Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi; the attacking line was led by 1993 [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") winner [Roberto Baggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Baggio "Roberto Baggio") of [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus "Juventus"). Notable exclusions from Sacchi's _Azzurri_ selections included [Gianluca Vialli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluca_Vialli "Gianluca Vialli"), [Roberto Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini "Roberto Mancini"), [Giuseppe Bergomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe_Bergomi "Giuseppe Bergomi") (who had been part of the World Cup winning squad of [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup")) and [Walter Zenga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Zenga "Walter Zenga").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-10)

Sacchi led Italy through the [qualification campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(UEFA_%E2%80%93_Group_1) "1994 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA – Group 1)") to reach the [1994 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup "1994 FIFA World Cup"). Despite losing their first match 1–0 to the [Republic of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland_national_football_team "Republic of Ireland national football team") and finishing third in their group, Italy reached the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1994 FIFA World Cup final") (their first since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1982 FIFA World Cup final")), where they were defeated by [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"), the first ever shootout in a World Cup final. Under Sacchi, Italy qualified for [UEFA Euro 1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1996 "UEFA Euro 1996"), but were eliminated in the group stage from a group which included the eventual finalists, [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") and the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9) Sacchi later commented that the Euro 96 side were his best Italy team.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-11)

### Later coaching and executive career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Later coaching and executive career")]

After leaving his position with the national team, Sacchi returned to Milan to replace [Óscar Tabárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93scar_Tab%C3%A1rez "Óscar Tabárez") in December 1996. However, the second spell was unsuccessful with Milan finishing 11th in [the league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_Serie_A "1996–97 Serie A") and suffering its worst ever Serie A defeat, losing 6–1 at home to eventual champions Juventus.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9)

Sacchi had brief spells in the Spanish [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), taking charge of [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in 1998 after his second spell with the _Rossoneri_, where he left his post in March of that season, with them languishing in the bottom half of the table. He also briefly returned to Parma in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_Serie_A "2000–01 Serie A"), replacing [Alberto Malesani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Malesani "Alberto Malesani"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9) but resigned after only 3 matches (2 draws, 1 victory) for stress reasons, to be replaced by [Renzo Ulivieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renzo_Ulivieri "Renzo Ulivieri").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-12) He later returned to Madrid, this time at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") as director of football at [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid") for the [2004–05 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Real_Madrid_C.F._season "2004–05 Real Madrid C.F. season").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-13)

## Management style, reception, and influence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Management style, reception, and influence")]

Nicknamed "The Prophet of Fusignano",[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-14) Sacchi is regarded as one of the greatest managers of all time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatestmanagers-2) He favored a fluid, yet highly organised attacking [4–4–2 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%934%E2%80%932 "Formation (association football)"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatest-16) discarding the traditional [libero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libero_(football) "Libero (football)")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17) in an era where Italian football was mainly focussed on strong defensive play,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatest-16)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-revolution-18) and [Helenio Herrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helenio_Herrera "Helenio Herrera")'s _[Catenaccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catenaccio "Catenaccio")_ tactics were still a strong influence.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17) Defensively, Sacchi's teams adopted a [zonal marking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marking_(association_football)#Zonal_marking "Marking (association football)") system, which had already been introduced by his predecessor [Nils Liedholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils_Liedholm "Nils Liedholm"), and were known for their defensive strength, conceding few goals;[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-Game_Changers-19) indeed, the defensive quartet of Maldini, Baresi, Costacurta, and Tassotti, which Sacchi deployed both at Milan and with the Italy national team, is regarded as one of the greatest defences of all-time.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-Game_Changers-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-23)

Sacchi believes in the Dutch concept of [Total Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Football "Total Football"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15) insisting that young players should be coached in all aspects of football rather than into specialist positions, helping the team both with or without the ball.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-magician-24) He is credited as an innovator, popularising high pressing from his teams, the [offside trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offside_(association_football)#Offside_trap "Offside (association football)"), and a high defensive line with no more than 25 metres between defence and attack.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-revolution-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-Game_Changers-19)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-magician-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-26) This style of pressing has been emulated successfully by [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho")'s [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-revolution-18)[Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola")'s [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15)[Jürgen Klopp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp "Jürgen Klopp")'s [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-27) and [Jupp Heynckes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupp_Heynckes "Jupp Heynckes")'s Bayern Munich.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-28) His successor at Milan, [Fabio Capello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Capello "Fabio Capello"), retained aspects of Sacchi's tactics and went on to win four _[Scudetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_Italian\_football\_champions "List of Italian football champions")_ in five seasons and the [1993–94 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993%E2%80%9394_UEFA_Champions_League "1993–94 UEFA Champions League").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatest-16) Spanish coach [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") cites Sacchi as his role model and "the coach who has revolutionised football in the past 50 years".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-29)

Sacchi was a firm believer in team ethic, work ethic, discipline and treating all players as equals,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-30) once saying, "The only way you can build a side is by getting players who speak the same language and can play a team game. You can't achieve anything on your own, and if you do, it doesn't last long. I often quote what [Michelangelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelangelo "Michelangelo") said: 'The spirit guides the hand.'"[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-said-31) To perfect his team's cohesion, Sacchi introduced "shadow play", where his players would simulate a match in training without a football.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17)

Sacchi also attracted controversy for implementing a strict and rigorous training regime for his players. Sacchi is also remembered for his outspokenness, stubbornness and his meticulous, obsessive attention to detail when preparing tactical solutions and perfecting plays, which his players were then expected to memorise and implement consistently during matches.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-32) Throughout his career, he clashed with several of his players, including [Marco Van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Van_Basten "Marco Van Basten"), [Gianluca Vialli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluca_Vialli "Gianluca Vialli"), and [Roberto Baggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Baggio "Roberto Baggio"), as well as manager [Fabio Capello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Capello "Fabio Capello").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-5_rivalit%C3%A0-36)

Sacchi has been frequently imitated in television by Italian comedian [Maurizio Crozza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurizio_Crozza "Maurizio Crozza").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-37)

**Arrigo Sacchi** (born 1 April 1946) is an Italian former [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") executive and manager, best known for having managed [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") and the [Italy national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"). Regarded as one of the greatest managers of all time,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatestmanagers-2) his Milan side (1987–1991) is widely regarded to be one of the greatest club squads of all time.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-5)

Sacchi won the [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") title in his [debut season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987%E2%80%9388_Serie_A "1987–88 Serie A") and then dominated European football by winning back to back [European Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_final "1989 European Cup final") and [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final "1990 European Cup final"). From 1991 to 1996, he was head coach of Italy and led them to the [1994 FIFA World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1994 FIFA World Cup final"), where they lost to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in a penalty shoot-out.

Sacchi was never a professional football player and, for many years, worked as a shoe salesman. This led to his famous quote directed at those who questioned his qualifications: "I never realised that in order to become a jockey you have to have been a horse first."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-No_experience_required-6) Another famous Sacchi quote is that "football is the most important of the least important things in life".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]

Sacchi had grown up watching attacking sides, such as [Budapest Honvéd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest_Honv%C3%A9d_FC "Budapest Honvéd FC"), [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F."), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") and the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team "Netherlands national football team"). He started his career managing his local club, Baracca Lugo, because he was not good enough to play for them. Of the challenge he faced, Sacchi said, "I was twenty-six, my goalkeeper was thirty-nine and my centre-forward was thirty-two. I had to win them over." He next coached at Bellaria before joining [Cesena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Cesena "AC Cesena"), who were in the [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B"), as a youth team coach. He then took over at [Rimini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimini_Calcio_FC "Rimini Calcio FC"), who were playing in the [Serie C1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_C1 "Serie C1"), and almost led them to a title.

He received his breakthrough when he moved to [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") as a youth coach. His achievements with the youth team earned interest from [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913"), who were then playing in Serie C1. He led Parma to promotion in his first season, and in the following season took them to within 3 points of promotion to [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A"). Of greater importance to his time at Parma, however, was the team's performance in the [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppa_Italia "Coppa Italia"); they beat [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") 1–0 in the group stages, and beat them again 1–0 on aggregate in the first knockout round. This was enough to attract interest from Milan club owner [Silvio Berlusconi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silvio_Berlusconi "Silvio Berlusconi"), who promptly appointed Sacchi as manager.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-gazzettadiparma-8)

### AC Milan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: AC Milan")]

In Milan, Sacchi again faced problems of credibility. The press argued that such an inadequate player could never go on to be a successful coach, and that even Berlusconi – who had played football at amateur level – was probably a better player. Sacchi wittily replied, "I never realised that in order to become a jockey you have to have been a horse first."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-No_experience_required-6) Sacchi was an instant success at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro"), leading Milan to its first [Serie A title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Italian_football_champions "List of Italian football champions") in nine years in his [debut season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987%E2%80%9388_Serie_A "1987–88 Serie A"), following up the league title with a [Supercoppa Italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercoppa_Italiana "Supercoppa Italiana") in [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Supercoppa_Italiana "1988 Supercoppa Italiana").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9)

Sacchi's success at Milan gained him two back-to-back [European Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9) The success he gained was largely attributed to the Dutch trio he had purchased: [Marco van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_van_Basten "Marco van Basten"), [Ruud Gullit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_Gullit "Ruud Gullit") and [Frank Rijkaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rijkaard "Frank Rijkaard"). However, other great players such as [Roberto Donadoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Donadoni "Roberto Donadoni"), as well as the defensive back four of [Franco Baresi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Baresi "Franco Baresi"), [Alessandro Costacurta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Costacurta "Alessandro Costacurta"), [Mauro Tassotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Tassotti "Mauro Tassotti") and [Paolo Maldini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Maldini "Paolo Maldini"), were also key to his success.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)

The first European Cup final in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_European_Cup_final "1989 European Cup final") was against [Steaua București](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Steaua_Bucure%C8%99ti "FC Steaua București"), who were beaten 4–0. Gullit and Van Basten scored two goals each and Milan lifted the [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988%E2%80%9389_European_Cup "1988–89 European Cup") for the first time in over 20 years. En route to the final, Milan had dispatched [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F.") 6–1 on aggregate in the semi-final. The quarter-final against [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen") was a tight affair; Milan only went through 1–0 on aggregate thanks to a Van Basten penalty. The second round was shrouded in controversy. Donadoni had his life saved only through the quick-thinking of the [Red Star Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Star_Belgrade "Red Star Belgrade") physio, who broke his jaw to make a passage for oxygen to reach his lungs after he had suffered a bad foul and lay unconscious. The first leg ended in a 1–1 draw, and the second leg was called off in the 64th minute and rescheduled to be replayed the next day due to the thick fog (Milan was losing 0–1 at the moment). Milan eventually progressed following a penalty shoot-out.

Although the team was not as strong as they had been in the previous season, they were victorious again in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_European_Cup "1989–90 European Cup"). After victories against [HJK Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsingin_Jalkapalloklubi "Helsingin Jalkapalloklubi"), Real Madrid and [KV Mechelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KV_Mechelen "KV Mechelen"), Milan defeated German [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") in the semi-final, thanks to an [away goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goal_rule "Away goal rule"). In the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final "1990 European Cup final") Frank Rijkaard scored the only goal of the game through a Van Basten assist to conquer [Sven-Göran Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven-G%C3%B6ran_Eriksson "Sven-Göran Eriksson")'s [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica"). By winning the final, Milan became the first team which retained the title since [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979%E2%80%9380_European_Cup "1979–80 European Cup"), and the last team to do so until Real Madrid would manage to achieve this feat 27 years later. Sacchi would also capture back to back [European Super Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup "UEFA Super Cup") and [Intercontinental Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960%E2%80%932004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") in 1989 and 1990, and would lead Milan to the final of the [1989–90 Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_Coppa_Italia "1989–90 Coppa Italia"), where they were defeated by [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC"). The following season saw them defeated by [eventual runners-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_European_Cup "1990–91 European Cup")[Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") in the quarter-final, and finish second in [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_Serie_A "1990–91 Serie A") behind [Sampdoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Sampdoria "UC Sampdoria"), while they were eliminated in the semi-finals of the [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990%E2%80%9391_Coppa_Italia "1990–91 Coppa Italia") by eventual champions [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma"). This was Sacchi's last season with _i Rossoneri_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9)

### Italy national team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Italy national team")]

In November 1991, Sacchi was appointed manager of the [Italy national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"), replacing [Azeglio Vicini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azeglio_Vicini "Azeglio Vicini"). Sacchi based his Italian selection predominantly on Milan players, especially in the defensive line, which featured Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi; the attacking line was led by 1993 [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") winner [Roberto Baggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Baggio "Roberto Baggio") of [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus "Juventus"). Notable exclusions from Sacchi's _Azzurri_ selections included [Gianluca Vialli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluca_Vialli "Gianluca Vialli"), [Roberto Mancini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini "Roberto Mancini"), [Giuseppe Bergomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe_Bergomi "Giuseppe Bergomi") (who had been part of the World Cup winning squad of [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup")) and [Walter Zenga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Zenga "Walter Zenga").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-10)

Sacchi led Italy through the [qualification campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(UEFA_%E2%80%93_Group_1) "1994 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA – Group 1)") to reach the [1994 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup "1994 FIFA World Cup"). Despite losing their first match 1–0 to the [Republic of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland_national_football_team "Republic of Ireland national football team") and finishing third in their group, Italy reached the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1994 FIFA World Cup final") (their first since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1982 FIFA World Cup final")), where they were defeated by [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"), the first ever shootout in a World Cup final. Under Sacchi, Italy qualified for [UEFA Euro 1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1996 "UEFA Euro 1996"), but were eliminated in the group stage from a group which included the eventual finalists, [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") and the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9) Sacchi later commented that the Euro 96 side were his best Italy team.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-11)

### Later coaching and executive career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Later coaching and executive career")]

After leaving his position with the national team, Sacchi returned to Milan to replace [Óscar Tabárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93scar_Tab%C3%A1rez "Óscar Tabárez") in December 1996. However, the second spell was unsuccessful with Milan finishing 11th in [the league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_Serie_A "1996–97 Serie A") and suffering its worst ever Serie A defeat, losing 6–1 at home to eventual champions Juventus.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9)

Sacchi had brief spells in the Spanish [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), taking charge of [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in 1998 after his second spell with the _Rossoneri_, where he left his post in March of that season, with them languishing in the bottom half of the table. He also briefly returned to Parma in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_Serie_A "2000–01 Serie A"), replacing [Alberto Malesani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Malesani "Alberto Malesani"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-SacchitakeoverParma-9) but resigned after only 3 matches (2 draws, 1 victory) for stress reasons, to be replaced by [Renzo Ulivieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renzo_Ulivieri "Renzo Ulivieri").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-12) He later returned to Madrid, this time at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium") as director of football at [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid") for the [2004–05 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Real_Madrid_C.F._season "2004–05 Real Madrid C.F. season").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-13)

## Management style, reception, and influence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arrigo_Sacchi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Management style, reception, and influence")]

Nicknamed "The Prophet of Fusignano",[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-14) Sacchi is regarded as one of the greatest managers of all time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatestmanagers-2) He favored a fluid, yet highly organised attacking [4–4–2 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4%E2%80%934%E2%80%932 "Formation (association football)"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatest-16) discarding the traditional [libero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libero_(football) "Libero (football)")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17) in an era where Italian football was mainly focussed on strong defensive play,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatest-16)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-revolution-18) and [Helenio Herrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helenio_Herrera "Helenio Herrera")'s _[Catenaccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catenaccio "Catenaccio")_ tactics were still a strong influence.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17) Defensively, Sacchi's teams adopted a [zonal marking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marking_(association_football)#Zonal_marking "Marking (association football)") system, which had already been introduced by his predecessor [Nils Liedholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils_Liedholm "Nils Liedholm"), and were known for their defensive strength, conceding few goals;[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-Game_Changers-19) indeed, the defensive quartet of Maldini, Baresi, Costacurta, and Tassotti, which Sacchi deployed both at Milan and with the Italy national team, is regarded as one of the greatest defences of all-time.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-Game_Changers-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-23)

Sacchi believes in the Dutch concept of [Total Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Football "Total Football"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15) insisting that young players should be coached in all aspects of football rather than into specialist positions, helping the team both with or without the ball.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-magician-24) He is credited as an innovator, popularising high pressing from his teams, the [offside trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offside_(association_football)#Offside_trap "Offside (association football)"), and a high defensive line with no more than 25 metres between defence and attack.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-The_greatest_teams_of_all_time:_AC_Milan_1988-90-4)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-revolution-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-Game_Changers-19)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-magician-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-26) This style of pressing has been emulated successfully by [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho")'s [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Porto "FC Porto"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-revolution-18)[Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola")'s [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-90s-15)[Jürgen Klopp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp "Jürgen Klopp")'s [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-27) and [Jupp Heynckes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupp_Heynckes "Jupp Heynckes")'s Bayern Munich.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-28) His successor at Milan, [Fabio Capello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Capello "Fabio Capello"), retained aspects of Sacchi's tactics and went on to win four _[Scudetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_Italian\_football\_champions "List of Italian football champions")_ in five seasons and the [1993–94 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993%E2%80%9394_UEFA_Champions_League "1993–94 UEFA Champions League").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-greatest-16) Spanish coach [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") cites Sacchi as his role model and "the coach who has revolutionised football in the past 50 years".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-29)

Sacchi was a firm believer in team ethic, work ethic, discipline and treating all players as equals,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-30) once saying, "The only way you can build a side is by getting players who speak the same language and can play a team game. You can't achieve anything on your own, and if you do, it doesn't last long. I often quote what [Michelangelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelangelo "Michelangelo") said: 'The spirit guides the hand.'"[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-said-31) To perfect his team's cohesion, Sacchi introduced "shadow play", where his players would simulate a match in training without a football.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-breaking-17)

Sacchi also attracted controversy for implementing a strict and rigorous training regime for his players. Sacchi is also remembered for his outspokenness, stubbornness and his meticulous, obsessive attention to detail when preparing tactical solutions and perfecting plays, which his players were then expected to memorise and implement consistently during matches.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-32) Throughout his career, he clashed with several of his players, including [Marco Van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Van_Basten "Marco Van Basten"), [Gianluca Vialli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluca_Vialli "Gianluca Vialli"), and [Roberto Baggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Baggio "Roberto Baggio"), as well as manager [Fabio Capello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Capello "Fabio Capello").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-5_rivalit%C3%A0-36)

Sacchi has been frequently imitated in television by Italian comedian [Maurizio Crozza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurizio_Crozza "Maurizio Crozza").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrigo_Sacchi#cite_note-37)

The **1990 European Cup final** was a [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match between title holders [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") of Italy and [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") of Portugal, played on 23 May 1990 at the [Praterstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst-Happel-Stadion "Ernst-Happel-Stadion") in [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), Austria. The winning goal came for Milan in the 68th minute, when [Frank Rijkaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rijkaard "Frank Rijkaard") ran through the opposing defence and scored the only goal of the match.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

Milan were the last club until [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2017 UEFA Champions League final") to successfully defend their title.

The **1990 European Cup final** was a [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match between title holders [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") of Italy and [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica") of Portugal, played on 23 May 1990 at the [Praterstadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst-Happel-Stadion "Ernst-Happel-Stadion") in [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), Austria. The winning goal came for Milan in the 68th minute, when [Frank Rijkaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rijkaard "Frank Rijkaard") ran through the opposing defence and scored the only goal of the match.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

Milan were the last club until [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2017 UEFA Champions League final") to successfully defend their title.

**Helmut Kohl** (8 February 1943 – 26 September 1991) was an Austrian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football")[referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") who officiated three matches in the [1990 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup") in Italy and the [1990 European Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_Final "1990 European Cup Final"). He died little over a year later at the age of 48.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Kohl_(referee)#cite_note-1)

**Helmut Kohl** (8 February 1943 – 26 September 1991) was an Austrian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football")[referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)") who officiated three matches in the [1990 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup") in Italy and the [1990 European Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_European_Cup_Final "1990 European Cup Final"). He died little over a year later at the age of 48.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Kohl_(referee)#cite_note-1)
