### Team selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Team selection")]

[![Image 40: A man with red hair, wearing a red football shirt and white shorts.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/P_Scholes.jpg/250px-P_Scholes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P_Scholes.jpg)

[![Image 41: A man with dark hair and stubble, wearing a red jacket with grey sleeves.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Roy_Keane_cropped.jpg/250px-Roy_Keane_cropped.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Roy_Keane_cropped.jpg)

Midfielders [Paul Scholes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Scholes "Paul Scholes") (left) and [Roy Keane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Keane "Roy Keane") were both suspended for the final.

Manchester United left England two days before the final, first flying from [Manchester Ringway Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Airport "Manchester Airport") to [Heathrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Heathrow_Airport "London Heathrow Airport"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Ferris-12):328 where they boarded a [Concorde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concorde "Concorde") aircraft for the flight to Barcelona.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-55) They stayed in the Meliá Gran hotel in the town of [Sitges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitges "Sitges"), about 20 miles (32 kilometres) down the coast south-west of Barcelona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Ferris-12):332 Captain Roy Keane and midfielder Paul Scholes both missed out on the final due to suspension; manager [Alex Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Ferguson "Alex Ferguson") had originally considered selecting Giggs to join [Nicky Butt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicky_Butt "Nicky Butt") in central midfield, but ultimately picked [David Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Beckham "David Beckham") as a player who could help the team control possession in the middle of the pitch,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Ferris-12):327 with Giggs on the right wing and [Jesper Blomqvist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesper_Blomqvist "Jesper Blomqvist") starting on the left.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Ferris-12):338 Keane had suffered an ankle injury in the FA Cup final that would keep him out until the start of the following season,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-56) but his suspension rendered the injury irrelevant to his selection.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-57) Norwegian defender [Henning Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henning_Berg "Henning Berg") also missed out through injury, meaning that his compatriot [Ronny Johnsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronny_Johnsen "Ronny Johnsen")—who had been an early contender to play alongside Butt in midfield[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-58)—played in central defence alongside [Jaap Stam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaap_Stam "Jaap Stam"), who overcame an [Achilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon") injury.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-59) With Keane out, goalkeeper Schmeichel—who in November 1998 had announced his intention to leave Manchester United at the end of the season[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-60)—was named as captain for his final Manchester United appearance;[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-schmeichel_bang-61) this meant that both sides were captained by their goalkeepers, as [Oliver Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Kahn "Oliver Kahn") wore the armband for Bayern.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-aizelwood-62) As Manchester United's top two goalscorers throughout the season, Cole and Yorke started up front, leaving Sheringham—who had played a part in both goals in the FA Cup Final a few days earlier—on the bench. Also on the bench were fellow striker [Ole Gunnar Solskjær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Gunnar_Solskj%C3%A6r "Ole Gunnar Solskjær"), back-up goalkeeper [Raimond van der Gouw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raimond_van_der_Gouw "Raimond van der Gouw"), defenders [David May](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_May_(footballer) "David May (footballer)"), [Phil Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Neville "Phil Neville") and [Wes Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brown "Wes Brown"), and midfielder [Jonathan Greening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Greening "Jonathan Greening").

Bayern coach [Ottmar Hitzfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottmar_Hitzfeld "Ottmar Hitzfeld") announced his team's line-up for the final two full days ahead of the match.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bayern_lineup-63) Injuries also impacted on his selections, with French left-back [Bixente Lizarazu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bixente_Lizarazu "Bixente Lizarazu") and Brazilian forward Élber having suffered season-ending knee injuries.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-65) Élber's absence resulted in Bayern playing a three-man attack of Basler, Jancker and Zickler, while Lizarazu was replaced on the left flank by [Michael Tarnat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Tarnat "Michael Tarnat") playing in a wing-back role opposite [Markus Babbel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_Babbel "Markus Babbel") on the right.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-66) Babbel was originally intended to play a man-marking role on Giggs, with his defensive abilities earning him selection ahead of the more attack-minded [Thomas Strunz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Strunz "Thomas Strunz");[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-bayern_lineup-63) however, this was nullified by Giggs' selection on the right wing, where he would play against Tarnat. The Bayern defence was anchored around sweeper Matthäus, who played behind [Thomas Linke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Linke "Thomas Linke") and Ghana international [Samuel Kuffour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Kuffour "Samuel Kuffour") – the only non-German in the Bayern side (by comparison, Manchester United had four Englishmen in their team); Linke and Kuffour's partnership at centre-back meant club captain [Thomas Helmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Helmer "Thomas Helmer") had to settle for a place on the bench.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-aizelwood-62) Effenberg and [Jens Jeremies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Jeremies "Jens Jeremies") played in central midfield for Bayern, with Jeremies man-marking Beckham.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-67)

### Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Summary")]

#### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_Final_teams_line_up.jpg/250px-1999_UEFA_Champions_League_Final_teams_line_up.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1999_UEFA_Champions_League_Final_teams_line_up.jpg)

The teams line up ahead of kick-off.

Six minutes into the match, Johnsen fouled Bayern striker Jancker just outside the area,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) and Basler placed a low free kick around the United wall to score the first goal, as Schmeichel was caught flat-footed.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) Although they were now a goal down, United began to dominate possession, but failed to create any clear-cut chances. The Bayern defence remained strong and well-organised, as Cole found out when his close-range effort was quickly closed down by three defenders.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) As Bayern began to look increasingly dangerous on the counter-attack than their opponents did in possession, Jancker repeatedly tested the United back four with a number of clever runs, some of which were flagged offside.

Cole once again found himself with a chance in the Bayern box, but goalkeeper Kahn hurried out of his goal to punch the ball to safety. At the other end, Basler came close with another free kick before Zickler sent a shot just wide from the edge of the box. As half-time approached, United winger Giggs, playing out of position on the right, sent a weak header towards Kahn from a Cole cross, but that was as close as they were to come to a goal in the first half.

#### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Second half")]

The German team started the second half in a more positive mood, with Jancker forcing a save from Schmeichel within a minute after the restart.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) Basler was proving to be Bayern's most dangerous player, first firing a 30-yard shot towards goal and then setting up a header for Babbel, who missed the ball entirely. United put together an attack when, after a healthy period of possession, Giggs crossed towards Blomqvist, who could only knock the ball over the bar after a desperate stretch.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) Another chance for Basler prompted Ferguson to bring on Sheringham for Blomqvist which resulted in a return to the more common formation of Giggs on the left (having started right-wing), with Beckham moving from an uncommon central to his more familiar right midfield position. Yorke dropped further back into a central midfield position.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) Hitzfeld responded with a substitution of his own, bringing on [Mehmet Scholl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehmet_Scholl "Mehmet Scholl"), who immediately set up Effenberg for a long-range shot that went narrowly wide. Schmeichel kept his side in the game when tipping another Effenberg shot over the bar after 75 minutes.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-wheeler-69) Scholl then almost scored from a delicate 20-yard chip after a run from Basler, but the ball bounced back off the post and into Schmeichel's arms.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) With the game seemingly drifting away from the English side, Ferguson introduced Solskjær to replace Cole with 10 minutes remaining.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-wheeler-69) The substitute immediately forced Kahn into a diving save with a header; it was the closest United had come to scoring all game.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) A minute later, Bayern missed a chance to secure the trophy, when an [overhead kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_kick "Bicycle kick") from Jancker came off the crossbar.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-key_moments-68) As the game crept into the last five minutes, United's two substitutes forced Kahn into more saves, firstly through a Sheringham volley and then from another Solskjær header.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-70)

##### Injury time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Injury time")]

> Beckham, in towards Schmeichel. It's come for Dwight Yorke. Cleared... Giggs with the shot, _Sheringham!_ Name on the trophy! Teddy Sheringham, with 30 seconds of added time played, has equalised for Manchester United – they are _still_ in the European Cup!

—[Clive Tyldesley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clive_Tyldesley "Clive Tyldesley") on [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)")'s broadcast call of Sheringham's injury time equaliser[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-The_Commentator's_Tale-71)

United won a corner when Effenberg deflected Gary Neville's cross over the Bayern goal line just as the [fourth official](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_referee_(association_football)#Fourth_official "Assistant referee (association football)") indicated three minutes of injury time. With so little time left for an equaliser, Schmeichel ventured up to Bayern's [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area"). Beckham flighted the corner in just over Schmeichel's head, Yorke put the ball back towards the crowded area, and after Fink failed to clear sufficiently, the ball arrived at the feet of Giggs on the edge of the area. His right-footed snap-shot was weak and poorly struck, but it went straight to Sheringham, who swiped at the shot with his right foot, and nestled the ball in the bottom corner of the net. The goal was timed at 36 seconds into injury time.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-72) It looked as if, having been behind for most of the match, United had forced extra time.

> You have to feel this is their year. Is this their moment? Beckham, into Sheringham – _and Solskjær has won it!_ Manchester United have reached the promised land! Ole Solskjær! The two substitutes have scored the two goals in stoppage time and the treble looms large!

—Tyldesley on ITV's broadcast of Solskjær's injury time winner[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-The_Commentator's_Tale-71)

Less than 30 seconds after the subsequent kick-off, United forced another corner when Kuffour deflected Solskjær's cross over the Bayern goal line, but Schmeichel stayed in his penalty area this time, under instruction from Ferguson. Beckham again swung the corner in, finding the head of Sheringham, who nodded the ball down across the face of goal. Solskjær reacted fastest, stuck out a foot and poked the ball into the roof of the Bayern goal for United to take the lead with just 43 seconds of the three minutes of injury time to play. Solskjær celebrated by sliding on his knees, mimicking Basler's earlier celebration, before quickly being mobbed by the United players, substitutes and coaching staff.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-73) Schmeichel, in his own penalty area, cartwheeled with glee.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-74)

The game restarted, but many Bayern players were overwhelmed with despair, virtually unable to continue and needed the assistance of referee Collina to drag themselves off the ground.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-75) They were stunned to have lost a game they had thought won just minutes before; several celebratory flares had already been ignited by the Bayern fans moments before United equalised, and ribbons in the club's colours had already been secured to the trophy in preparation for the presentation ceremony.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-76) United held onto their lead to record their second European Cup title,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-77) and at the final whistle, referee Collina described the cheers from the fans as being like a "lion's roar".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-78) Kuffour broke down in tears after the game, beating the floor in despair, and Jancker collapsed in anguish.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-79) Matthäus had captained Bayern in the [1987 European Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_European_Cup_final "1987 European Cup final") and lost in similar circumstances to two late Porto goals. He had been substituted with 10 minutes remaining, with victory seemingly assured.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-mirror-80)
